title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that compares ungated LLM generation to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline applied to a single shared LLM candidate per intent. Generation requested gpt-5-mini; the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤ 1 (no extra LLM calls). Primary, artifact-backed outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We additionally report the confirmatory bank difficulty-label aggregation (easy=20, medium=80, hard=60, very_hard=40) and an auditable exemplar of the single repaired episode (task_id task-000137; validator violation MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND; deterministic repair = canonical insertion of the missing required command; validation_before.valid == false → validation_after.valid == true). All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and question. Large language models (LLMs) can automate routine network-operations (NetOps) tasks such as translating an operator intent into device configuration, but generated artifacts risk structural or semantic errors that may break control-plane behavior when applied. Prior prototype work demonstrates the feasibility of intent-to-configuration translation while documenting failure modes such as missing required commands, ordering errors, or inadvertent modification of protected fields; mitigation proposals include constrained decoding, retrieval augmentation, and verifier-assisted repair. However, operational constraints—hosted-model call budgets, governance, and auditability—create a pragmatic question: given a single initial LLM candidate per intent, does applying a conservative, deterministic generate–verify–repair guard meaningfully increase the rate of emulator-executable configurations?

Study framing and contribution. We preregistered and executed a paired, shared-initial-generation confirmatory experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) designed to isolate the marginal effect of a deterministic, auditable repair applied only to the original candidate. The paired shared-candidate estimand answers a practical deployment question: when model calls are costly or restricted, can an inexpensive deterministic validator plus a single rule-based repair (if unambiguous) improve operational yield without additional LLM invocations? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under this shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise, auditable descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and deterministic repair operator; (3) exact small-sample inference and bootstrap uncertainty quantification appropriate for discordant-pair analysis; and (4) artifact-grounded clarifications requested during review (difficulty-label aggregate and a single repaired-episode exemplar). The conservative design and artifact-rich execution aim to support operational interpretation rather than to claim broad production generality.
sections.related_work:
Three literatures motivate and contextualize this study. First, intent-to-configuration and LLM-for-NetOps prototypes demonstrate that LLMs can synthesize vendor-like CLI sequences but that correctness problems remain unless outputs are post-processed; representative empirical evaluations and surveys document both promise and structured-output failure modes (e.g., Nguyen et al., 2024; multiple recent surveys and prototype reports in the evidence corpus). This body establishes that generated configurations frequently require downstream assurance mechanisms to be safe for application.

Second, mitigation strategies from NetOps and adjacent structured-generation domains include retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), live schema grounding (SAL), grammar- and constraint-aware decoding, and verifier-assisted repair. Work in NL2SQL and schema-aware generation shows that grounding and post-generation verification reduce hallucination and format errors, but these methods require careful adaptation for vendor CLI dialects and operational policies (e.g., SAL and constrained-decoding references in the evidence bundle). These approaches trade off provider-call cost, latency, and audit complexity against improved structural accuracy.

Third, deterministic verifiers and emulator-backed validators are natural assurance layers: formal-methods tools and NetKAT variants, and weighted/ensemble verification work, can check reachability and structural invariants and provide machine-readable violation types suitable for automated repair. The literature also emphasizes verification limits: emulators and formal abstractions are useful for pre-deployment checks but do not fully capture dynamic runtime behaviors such as convergence timing or vendor firmware idiosyncrasies. Our study intentionally situates itself at the intersection of these strands by empirically measuring the marginal yield of a conservative GVR guard when model-call budgets are restricted to a single initial generation per intent.
sections.methodology:
Design overview and estimand. We preregistered a paired confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of 200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate configuration; that same candidate served both as the baseline (ungated acceptance) and as the guarded input to a deterministic generate–verify–repair pipeline. The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); the preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar (implemented as a two-sided binomial test on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared initial generations + 1 deterministic repair invocation implemented in code rather than additional LLM calls).

Task bank, scoring, and difficulty stratification. The confirmatory bank (n=200) was produced by a deterministic task generator; each payload encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (authoritative ordered command list), workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break), and difficulty metadata. The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires syntactic parseability, correct presence and order of required_sequence, enforcement of dependency/group policies, preservation of protected-interface values, and exact equality of the emulator-observed final_state to the expected_final_state. Reviewer-requested aggregated difficulty-label counts for the confirmatory bank are: easy=20, medium=80, hard=60, very_hard=40. These counts describe the stratified confirmatory distribution used in the paired experiment; full per-task labels and payloads are archived for inspection.

Deterministic validator and repair operator. The validator executes three deterministic stages: (1) syntactic parsing and canonical normalization (syntax failures emit SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR and block deterministic repair), (2) structural/workflow checks that deterministically verify presence and ordering of required_sequence and dependency rules (violation codes include MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION), and (3) deterministic emulator application (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) with final_state comparison. The validator emits machine-readable traces consumed by repair logic and the scorer (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, violation_codes, validation_before/after summaries).

The preregistered repair operator is a deterministic, rule-based transformer invoked only when (a) violation_count > 0, (b) the violation family is in a preregistered repairable set, and (c) an unambiguous canonical transformation can be computed from the task payload. Repairs obey constraints: (i) no extra LLM calls (repairs implemented by code), (ii) repair_budget ≤ 1 per episode for confirmatory runs, and (iii) abstention when multiple plausible deterministic repairs exist. Canonical mappings include insertion of missing required commands at manifest-specified positions, stable reordering to satisfy dependency constraints, and enforcement preserving protected fields. All repair decisions and resulting normalized configurations were recorded in audit traces.

Analysis procedures and pre-specified inference. The preregistered primary test is the exact McNemar (two-sided binomial on discordant pairs). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729) confined to the paired difference estimator. Missingness and provider-failure policies were prespecified: provider/API generation failures count as arm failures; none occurred in the confirmatory run. All analysis code, seeds, and artifacts are archived.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary outcomes. The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 paired episodes) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level counts: baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency derived from per-episode scoring is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and interval estimates. Applying the preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test (two-sided binomial on discordant pairs) to the observed discordant count n = n10 + n01 = 1 with k = n10 = 1 produces a two-sided p-value p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) yields a 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. Because the preregistered target absolute effect (0.15) is well outside the observed CI, the confirmatory data do not support that magnitude of improvement under the shared-candidate estimand given this task distribution.

Repair and failure diagnostics. Validator traces show validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1. That single deterministic repair converted the episode into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). No syntactic/parse failures or provider-call timeouts occurred. Provider-call accounting recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage invocations implemented by deterministic code = 1).

Artifact-grounded clarifications. Aggregated difficulty-label counts across the confirmatory bank: easy = 20, medium = 80, hard = 60, very_hard = 40. Auditable exemplar: the single repaired episode corresponds to task_id task-000137 in the archived manifest. In that episode the validator reported violation_codes = ["MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND"] and violation_count = 1. The deterministic repair applied the canonical Insertion transformation (inserting the missing required command at the canonical position derived from required_sequence). Post-repair the validator observed validation_after.valid == true and the normalized configuration passed the full intent constraints; the pre- and post-repair normalized configurations and the repair trace are preserved in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation for constrained deployments. Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic, auditable validators produce structured violation codes that enable targeted deterministic repairs; in this low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair applied to the same candidate is therefore small (one additional pass). For operators constrained by hosted-call budgets and requiring auditable decision chains, the guarded shared-candidate design provides an assurance gate with negligible additional provider cost.

Statistical sensitivity and design trade-offs. The exact McNemar is the appropriate small-sample paired test here; with observed discordant count n = 1 the two-sided p-value equals 1.0 and the chi-squared approximation would be invalid. The paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] further bounds plausible paired differences. Practically, near-ceiling baselines reduce discordant-pair counts and thus the sensitivity to moderate absolute improvements: detecting a 0.15 absolute difference with power would require a different baseline rate, a larger sample, or a task bank deliberately enriched for failure-prone intents.

Failure modes, abstention policy, and auditability. The deterministic repair operator is intentionally conservative: it applies only when a unique canonical transformation is computable from the task payload and abstains otherwise. This abstention policy prevents arbitrary or risky automatic changes when multiple plausible repairs exist and preserves auditability by recording explicit transformation decisions. The single successful repair in our run exemplifies the utility of deterministic violation codes (MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND) that map directly to simple, verifiable transformations (canonical insertion). For contexts where higher pass rates are required, independent resampling (multiple independent LLM draws per intent) or LLM-invoked repair loops could increase yield but at increased provider cost and greater governance complexity.

Threats to validity and generalization. Internal validity for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring is strong because of deterministic task generation, scoring, and emulator application. Construct validity is limited by emulator fidelity: while Mininet+FRR provides deterministic control-plane simulation, it cannot fully represent real-world dynamic behaviours such as BGP convergence timing or vendor firmware idiosyncrasies. External validity is restricted by the single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and by the synthetic curated task bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; extrapolation to multivendor CLI diversity, large-scale change workflows, or adversarial intents is therefore limited. Conclusion validity is constrained by the near-ceiling baseline reducing discordant pairs; the exact McNemar test is appropriate but has limited power when n is small. These limitations define where deterministic GVR guards are likely most useful (low-error, cost-constrained, audit-critical settings) and where additional designs (resampling, LLM-in-the-loop repair) warrant study.

Operational implications and guidance. Execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1; completed_episodes = 400) supports simple cost-versus-yield comparisons for operators choosing between shared-candidate guarded designs and multi-call strategies. Deterministic validators should be standard assurance machinery where auditable, repeatable checks and low-latency failure explanations are required. Where production deployments prioritize maximizing pass rates over minimizing provider calls, designers should evaluate independent-resampling, LLM-guided iterative repair, or constrained-decoding approaches while accounting for increased call budgets and governance burdens.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and task distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded negligible marginal improvement, but deterministic validators remain valuable, auditable assurance gates in operational NetOps pipelines. The full archived evidence bundle contains run traces and artifacts for independent audit and reanalysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: Generation requested gpt-5-mini. Validation used a deterministic netops validator implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by the study adapter. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤ 1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting: the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage invocations = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator and validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.
Full per-task difficulty labels and all run traces are archived in the study evidence bundle for audit and per-task inspection.
